introduction:
A Marriage Certificate in Maharashtra is a vital legal document that serves as definitive proof of marriage. It is officially registered by the Marriage Registrar under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 or the Special Marriage Act, 1954.

Obtaining a marriage certificate is essential for various legal procedures, including applying for a passport, opening joint bank accounts, claiming life insurance benefits, and establishing spousal rights.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Purpose: Applying for a Marriage Certificate in Maharashtra.
  • Official Portal: igrmaharashtra.gov.in via the e-Marriage 2.0 system.
  • Processing Time: The certificate is generally issued within 15 days of applying.
  • Application Fee: ₹150 for the online application process.
  • Witnesses: 3 witnesses are strictly required for the registration.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: Keep the original and photocopies of the following documents ready before registration.
For the Bride & Groom
  • Age Proof (Any one): Birth Certificate, School Leaving Certificate (Bonafide/SSC Exam Certificate), or Passport.
  • Residence Proof (Any one): Aadhaar Card, Passport, Election Card (Voter ID), Electricity Bill, Driving License, etc.
  • Marriage Proof: Original Wedding Invitation Card and a joint Marriage Photograph from the wedding ceremony.
  • Signatures: Scanned copies of signatures of both the bride and groom.
For the Witnesses (3 persons)
  • Identity & Residence Proof: Aadhaar Card (The address entered in the application form must exactly match the address printed on their respective Aadhaar cards).
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Apply Online via e-Marriage 2.0 Portal

Follow these steps to apply for a marriage certificate online:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Visit Portal: Go to the official website igrmaharashtra.gov.in and click on नोंदणी व मुद्रांक विभाग.
  2. Navigate to e-Marriage: Click on विवाह नोंदणी 2.0 (ई-मॅरेज) to access the e-Marriage 2.0 portal.
  3. Register/Login: Click on "Register Here" to create a new account, then log in with your credentials.
  4. Create New Notice: Click on "New Notice (Application)" and fill in the Office Details. Select the Marriage Type (e.g., 'Form 16 Marriage' if already married), District, and the specific Office Name where you wish to register.
  5. Groom & Bride Details: Fill in the detailed forms for both the Groom and the Bride. Crucial Note: The "Present Address" for both the bride and the groom must be exactly the same. Entering different current addresses will result in rejection.
  6. Witness Details: Enter the details of the 3 witnesses. Ensure the address entered matches their Aadhaar cards exactly.
  7. Document Upload: Upload all the required documents, photos, and signatures in the specified formats.
  8. KYC Verification: Complete the KYC Details by verifying the Bride and Groom using Aadhaar OTP.
  9. Payment: Proceed to Payment Details and pay the ₹150 application fee online.
  10. Physical SRO Visit (Mandatory): After successful submission and payment, a date will be scheduled. The bride, groom, and all 3 witnesses must physically visit the selected Marriage Registrar's office on that date for biometric capture and physical document verification.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Apply Offline at Local Municipal/Registrar Office

You can register your marriage offline by following these municipal guidelines in Maharashtra:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Obtain Form: Obtain a physical copy of Form "D" (Memorandum of Marriage) from your local municipal ward office (e.g., BMC, PMC), Gram Panchayat, or download it from their respective municipal websites.
  2. Fill Out Form: Complete the form entirely with the details of the husband, wife, and three witnesses.
  3. Priest's Signature: If the marriage was a traditional or religious ceremony, the form must be signed by the priest who solemnized the wedding.
  4. Attach Documents: Attach photocopies (often required to be attested or true copies) of all required documents (age proof, address proof for the couple and witnesses, marriage photographs, and wedding invitation).
  5. Submission & Payment: Submit the physical application form and documents to your local ward office or local Registrar of Marriages and pay the designated fee at the counter.
  6. Appointment: You will be assigned an appointment date. The couple and all 3 witnesses must be physically present at the office on that date to sign the register in front of the Marriage Officer.
afterApplying:
After Applying — What Next?

Tracking Application

After submitting the online application, a GRN (Government Receipt Number) or Token Number is generated. You can track status in the "Application List" tab on your dashboard (initially showing "Data entry pending" or "Submitted").

Witness Presence (Important)

Ensure all 3 witnesses are guaranteed to be present on your scheduled verification date. If even one witness is absent, the registration process will be delayed, requiring rescheduling of the SRO visit.

Certificate Issuance

Once the physical verification and biometrics are successfully completed at the office, the official Marriage Certificate will be processed and issued.
